query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Rapid quenching via arc melting on a water‐cooled Cu hearth will stabilize a dual-phase microstructure (fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves) in FeCoNiTi high-entropy alloys, overcoming the coercivity limitation of single-phase fcc alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi (nominal 1:1:1:1) that normally exhibits a dual-phase microstructure containing a ferromagnetic fcc phase and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
generation.intervention: Apply rapid quenching using arc melting on a water-cooled Cu hearth to promote and stabilize the coexistence of the fcc and C14 phases. Include synthesis of a compositionally matched, C14-dominant variant (Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29) as a control sample.
generation.conditions: Magnetic measurements performed up to 400 K and over a range of temperatures to capture multiple magnetic transitions; electronic structure calculations to probe spin-polarized density of states and orbital moments.
generation.structural_mediator: A stabilized dual-phase structure where the fcc phase (approx. 21.3Fe-24.8Co-32.2Ni-21.6Ti) coexists with the C14 Laves phase (approx. 27.3Fe-26.6Co-17.4Ni-28.7Ti), enabling chemical segregation at the phase boundaries that facilitates interfacial magnetic interactions.
generation.mechanism: Antiferromagnetic coupling between the Fe/Co/Ni sublattice and the Ti sublattice, combined with enhanced orbital moment contributions in the fcc phase through interface interactions with the C14 phase, promotes domain wall pinning. This interface-induced pinning effect increases the coercive field beyond the typical <100 Oe observed in single-phase fcc alloys.
generation.predicted_outcome: The dual-phase alloy’s fcc component is predicted to exhibit a significantly enhanced coercive field (approximately 667 Oe at 400 K) along with distinct magnetic ordering transitions (e.g., near 1084 K and 168 K for the fcc phase, in addition to C14-related transitions around 214 K).
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or related high-entropy alloys with coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe and limited orbital moment contributions.
generation.boundary: This behavior is expected only in the presence of the dual-phase microstructure with the specific chemical segregation and interfacial interactions. Pure single-phase fcc or pure C14 variants are not anticipated to exhibit the same coercivity enhancement or multi-transition magnetic behavior.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of coercivity enhancement and precise magnetic transition temperatures may vary depending on synthesis conditions and phase purity. There is some uncertainty in the quantitative contribution of the orbital moment enhancement from the interfacial interactions.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy using rapid quenching on a water-cooled Cu hearth and a C14-dominant control alloy (Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29). Conduct hysteresis loop measurements and temperature-dependent magnetization studies to identify coercivity and distinct magnetic transitions. Compare the coercive fields and transition temperatures between the dual-phase alloy, the single-phase fcc baseline, and the C14 control.
measurements: Hysteresis loop measurements at various temperatures (up to 400 K) to determine the coercivity of the fcc phase within the dual-phase sample.
Temperature-dependent magnetization measurements to identify magnetic ordering transitions corresponding to both fcc and C14 phases.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dual-phase alloy does not exhibit a coercive field significantly exceeding 100 Oe (or fails to reach around 667 Oe at 400 K) and does not show the predicted distinct magnetic transitions relative to the control compounds, then the hypothesis is rejected.
